guide.title: Hero meeting guide
guide.lead: How the team runs the meeting, presents the formats and records everything in the minutes. Professional image, active listening, commercial clarity, formal record-keeping and relationship continuity.
guide.openCasting: Open the casting to start new minutes

purpose.title: 1. Purpose and stance
purpose.p1: The meeting is about relationship-building, mapping and creating opportunities. It is not a rushed conversation, a promise of hiring or just a sales presentation. The goal is to get to know the Hero, understand their positioning and find real ways to connect them with brands, events and projects.
purpose.p2: Every contact represents Groscove Group: the experience must convey organization, consistency, courtesy and confidence. The Hero ends the conversation knowing how we work, what information we need and what the next steps are.
purpose.central: Core message: we are building relationships with Heroes to understand how each profile connects with brands and opportunities in the current cycle and, above all, in next year's actions.
purpose.momentTitle: How to frame the current moment

moment.a: This year's calendar has already had actions and events. Since the relationship with part of the casting is starting now, the team is mapping things out during this period.
moment.b: The window from Black Friday to the end of the year is a period of getting closer, testing and reading opportunities.
moment.c: This work also prepares next year's relationships and campaigns.
moment.d: No opportunity is guaranteed: each brand has its own criteria, budget, deadlines and processes.

image.title: 2. Image and setting standards
image.lead: Before joining, check your appearance and your surroundings. Tap each item once it's ready.

presentation.title: Personal presentation
presentation.text: Well presented, appropriate clothing, well-groomed appearance and clean, manicured nails. Professionalism without losing naturalness.

place.title: Setting
place.text: A quiet, tidy place, with no people walking through and no noise. No interruptions and no visually cluttered surroundings.

background.title: Background
background.text: Preferably white or black, clean and neutral, with no objects that draw attention away.

light.title: Lighting
light.text: Soft front or side light, face visible. No backlighting, harsh shadows or dark image.

camera.title: Camera and audio
camera.text: Camera at eye level, steady framing, tested audio and a good connection.

attitude.title: Attitude
attitude.text: A smile, courtesy, active listening, attention to the Hero's name and a welcoming manner from start to finish.

image.brand: The look reinforces the Groscove Group brand: discretion, consistency, elegance and professionalism. The meeting is also a brand experience.

opening.title: 3. Opening and company introduction
opening.quote: “Thank you for taking the time to talk with us. The idea of this meeting is to get to know your work better and understand your interests, your content calendar and the brands you already have an affinity with. Groscove Group is building relationship opportunities between Heroes, brands, events and projects. We want to understand what makes sense for you and show how we can build this together.”

structure.a: Make it clear that you are part of the Groscove Group team and that you lead the relationship and the next steps.
structure.b: Introduce Jonathas Groscove as the group's founder. Execution and follow-through are handled by the professionals in each area.
structure.c: Stress that the Hero has a team to organize information, opportunities and next steps.
structure.d: Don't center everything on the founder or suggest that only he can solve things. Highlight the team and the formal channels.

opening.institutional: “Jonathas is the founder of Groscove Group, but the work happens through a team of professionals who follow every step. It is with us that you will structure information, opportunities and day-to-day next steps.”

formats.title: 4. The four ways of working
formats.lead: Present them clearly. The formats happen at different times and each action depends on alignment between the Hero, the brand, the scope, the budget and the formal agreement.

cpa.title: Format 1 — CPA: relationship, links and coupons
cpa.lead: Suggested first step to start or deepen the relationship with brands: understand how familiar the Hero is with products and brands, test communication and see how the audience responds.

points.a: Ask which brands the Hero already consumes, knows or uses in their routine.
points.b: Explore the Universes tab to find segments and brands that fit the profile.
points.c: Links and discount coupons can be sent for tests, depending on availability and each brand's rules.
points.d: The Hero works links and coupons into content that fits their editorial calendar, always following the brand's guidelines.
points.e: The brand looks at fit, content quality, audience interest and the available results.

cpa.important: CPA is not guaranteed fixed pay. Explain up front the attribution rule, which action counts, the measurement window, the percentage or amount and how payment works, according to what the brand formalizes.

publi.title: Format 2 — Sponsored post: paid campaign
publi.lead: Once it understands the Hero's communication, the team can present sponsored content opportunities. Many brands need to know the profile and review the data before defining scope and investment.

points.a: Ask for the updated media kit by e-mail. If there is no media kit, ask for the data so the team can prepare an internal presentation.
points.b: Ask about past campaigns, brands served, formats delivered, results and the fees charged or desired.
points.c: Fees and terms depend on the brief, deliverables, deadline, usage rights, exclusivity and the brand's budget.

publi.important: Don't promise fees, campaigns or approval in the meeting. The proposal is handled and formalized by e-mail.

project.title: Format 3 — Original projects and sponsorship
project.lead: Groscove Group also looks for Heroes with their own ideas: projects, experiences, events, recurring formats or content properties that attract sponsors. References just to illustrate: Rancho do Carlinhos Maia, Farofa da Gkay, Neymar's charity auction, Ensaios da Anitta, Numanice da Ludmilla and Tardezinha do Thiaguinho. It's not about comparing scale or promising results.

points.a: Ask whether they have an idea on hold, a project in development or a community they'd like to bring together in an experience.
points.b: Listen without interrupting: concept, audience, format, place, calendar, differentiators, partners and stage.
points.c: Ask for the idea to be formalized by e-mail, even at an early stage.
points.d: The team can study the project and look for sponsors. Sponsorship tiers can exceed R$100k, depending on the project, scope and opportunity.

project.important: Don't promise sponsorship or amounts. The figure is a reference for the type of opportunity, not a guarantee: it depends on the pitch, budget, audience, what is offered in return and sponsor interest.

events.title: Format 4 — Brand events and experiences
events.lead: Brands and partners hire Heroes for events, activations, launches, internal meetings and experiences: relationships, content production and getting closer to the market.

points.a: Ask about availability, interest in events, the cities they can be in and how much notice they need.
points.b: Go over the participation formats: attendance, coverage, stories, reels, interviews, content before or after the event.
points.c: Opportunities can come from a brand or from the holding company's relationships with PR agencies and partners.
points.d: Stress punctuality, professional conduct, courtesy with staff and guests and keeping commitments.

events.important: No appearance is confirmed before alignment of brand, scope, fees, schedule and a formal agreement.

content.title: 5. Content that attracts brands
content.lead: Many Heroes want opportunities but don't keep up content that shows the brand their language, consistency and ability to communicate products. Handle the topic constructively, without judgment.

items.a: Naturalness: show products and experiences in a way that fits the routine, without turning everything into an ad.
items.b: Consistency: frequency and quality, without long gaps in posting when there is a calendar commitment.
items.c: Context: explain why they use, like or recommend something; show real use, benefit or experience.
items.d: Variety: short videos, stories, carousels, behind the scenes, tutorials, reviews and routine, according to the profile.
items.e: Community: start conversations, reply to comments and notice recurring questions.
items.f: Brand safety: care with language, image, information and transparency, labeling sponsored content.
items.g: Planning: connect commercial and seasonal dates to the Hero's segment, without artificial or out-of-context content.

content.calendar: The team sends a calendar of suggestions with relevant dates, seasonal opportunities and content ideas. It is a strategic reference: the Hero adapts it to their identity, schedule and production capacity.
content.universes: Advise the Hero to follow the Universes tab (segments and brands Groscove Group works with, always kept up to date) and to mark the universes that make sense, the brands they already know and the ones they want to explore. Marking something is not automatic campaign approval.

blackFriday.title: 6. Black Friday invitation
blackFriday.lead: In the meeting, present the Black Friday action and gauge the Hero's interest.
blackFriday.quote: “We are organizing a Black Friday initiative with a few brands and a structured content calendar. We want to understand whether you're interested in taking part and whether you can produce within the planned period and dates. The idea is to formalize the possibilities by e-mail early next week, with the details of each opportunity.”

points.a: Show the available calendar, with dates, formats and deadlines.
points.b: Ask about interest, availability and affinity with the brands or categories.
points.c: Record restrictions, conflicts with competitors, trips, commitments and formats they don't want to do.
points.d: Don't confirm participation before alignment of brand, scope, fees, availability and a formal agreement.

blackFriday.answers: Answers, from the portal and from the minutes, are kept together in the action's list.

questions.title: 7. Questions for a productive meeting
questions.lead: A two-way conversation: open questions, listening and recording what is concrete. Use them as a guide, not as an interrogation.

profile.title: Profile and positioning
profile.text: How do you define your content today? Which topics do you want to strengthen? Which audience do you want to reach? What sets your communication apart?

brands.title: Brands and affinity
brands.text: Which brands do you consume or admire? Which ones have you worked with? Are there segments you'd rather not promote? Are there contracts or exclusivities in force?

history.title: Commercial history
history.text: Have you done paid campaigns? Which formats did you deliver? What was the investment range or fee charged? What worked best? Can you show case studies or results?

audience.title: Metrics and audience
audience.text: What are your main channels? What are your audience's location, age range and profile? Which metrics can you share?

production.title: Production and schedule
production.text: How often do you post? How do you organize shooting and editing? Are there dates, trips or commitments that affect the calendar?

blackFriday.title: Black Friday
blackFriday.text: Are you interested in taking part? Which categories make sense? Can you meet the proposed calendar?

projects.title: Original projects
projects.text: Is there a project you'd like to get off the ground? What would the experience, audience, format, place and timeline be? What is already in place?

events.title: Events
events.text: Are you interested in appearances and activations? In which cities can you take part? Which delivery formats do you usually accept?

questions.noImprovise: If the answer isn't available yet, don't improvise: say the question will go to the responsible team and be answered by e-mail after internal validation.

mediaKit.title: 8. Media kit and profile details update
mediaKit.lead: At the end of the meeting, ask for the media kit by e-mail. If there's no ready-made document, ask for the information below so the team can put together the internal presentation and the pitch for brands.

items.identification: Identification: full name, stage name, city/state, short bio and professional contacts.
items.channels: Channels: links and @handles for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Twitch, website, podcast and other platforms.
items.audience: Audience: followers per channel, reach, impressions, average views, engagement and age, gender and location data.
items.content: Content: main topics and formats, frequency, differentiators and representative examples.
items.history: Commercial history: brands served, campaigns, deliverables, case studies, authorized results and testimonials.
items.prices: Formats and fees: stories, reels, feed, video, appearances, packages and reference ranges, if any.
items.conditions: Terms: availability, minimum lead times, travel, production costs, usage rights, paid boosting and exclusivity.
items.materials: Materials: professional photos, portraits, logo, portfolio and recent screenshots of insights.

mediaKit.registration: Full name and stage name, full address (for registration, shipping or logistics), phone or WhatsApp with area code, main and alternative e-mail, city and state. Confirm the spelling with the Hero.
mediaKit.sensitive: Bank details, documents and tax information only when needed, through the appropriate channel and with guidance from the responsible team. Never in a WhatsApp group or in open minutes.

items.a: E-mail is the official channel for brands, briefs, proposals, fees, approvals, contracts, deadlines and confirmations.
items.b: WhatsApp is for quick contact, alignments and notices, but it does not replace formalization by e-mail.
items.c: Advise the Hero to keep an eye on their inbox and spam folder.
items.d: After the meeting, the minutes go to the relevant internal groups and are sent to and filed in the Presidency's e-mail.
items.e: Standard e-mail subject: “{subject}”. The minutes on the platform already generate this subject.
items.f: Every action has an owner and a due date. Never leave a next step only in a stray message.

script.title: 10. Meeting script

prep.title: 1. Preparation
prep.do: Test camera, audio, lighting, background and connection, and open the materials.
prep.record: Date, time, participants and representative in charge (A).

welcome.title: 2. Welcome
welcome.do: Thank them, set a friendly tone and explain the purpose of the meeting.
welcome.record: Summary of the purpose and the context presented.

institutional.title: 3. Company overview
institutional.do: Introduce Groscove Group, the team, the founder's role and how the relationship works.

discovery.title: 4. Discovery
discovery.do: Learn about content, audience, brands, commercial history, schedule and preferences.
discovery.record: Answers, metrics, brands and restrictions (B and C).

formats.title: 5. Formats
formats.do: Explain CPA, sponsored posts, original projects and events, without promising hiring.
formats.record: Formats of interest and possibilities (D and F).

blackFriday.title: 6. Black Friday
blackFriday.do: Present the calendar and gauge interest and availability.

next.title: 7. Next steps
next.do: Ask for the media kit and data, update the profile details and agree on response deadlines.
next.record: Pending items, owners, due dates and response channel (G and I).

closing.title: 8. Closing
closing.do: Thank them, reinforce e-mail as the official channel and confirm what each party will send.
closing.record: Final summary and follow-up date (J and K).

script.tone: Friendliness and professionalism: genuine interest, camera on whenever possible, a smile, no interrupting and no side conversations. The quality of the relationship starts with how the Hero is welcomed.

items.a: Don't guarantee campaigns, fees, invitations, sponsorships, results or brand approval.
items.b: Don't say the Hero was approved by a brand just because they joined the casting or a selection.
items.c: Explain it correctly: the profile was included in the casting sent to advertisers for evaluation; each brand decides based on its own brief and criteria.
items.d: Don't assume that the lack of a general contract rules out every opportunity: each action can have its own negotiation and formal agreement.
items.e: Don't disclose confidential information about brands, other Heroes, fees or negotiations.
items.f: Don't advise publishing without a brief, authorization and agreed commercial terms.
items.g: When in doubt, record the question, forward it to the responsible team and answer by e-mail after validation.

minutes.title: 12. Meeting minutes (A to K)
minutes.text: Every meeting has minutes, filled in during the conversation or right after. Open them from the casting: Hero profile, Meetings tab, New minutes. Once finished, the minutes update the Hero's relationship, the answer to the open action, original projects and the calendar, and notify the owner of each next step.

after.title: 13. Post-meeting checklist
after.lead: Don't wrap up until it's all done. In the minutes, section K tracks each item and automatically checks off what the minutes themselves already answer.

items.a: Review the minutes: nothing ambiguous, no unauthorized promises.
items.c: Share in the internal groups for awareness and continuity.
items.d: Formally forward to the Presidency's e-mail for filing and record-keeping.
items.e: Ask by e-mail for the media kit or the pending data.
items.f: Update the Hero's details: name, address, phone and e-mail.
items.g: Send the calendar of suggestions and the agreed materials.
items.h: Record interest in CPA, sponsored posts, projects and events.
items.i: Forward unanswered questions to the right areas and track the replies by e-mail.
items.j: Set the follow-up owner and due date.

principle.title: Operating principle
principle.text: Relationships are built through consistency. Every meeting leaves the Hero well received, the team well informed and the operation with clear records. Groscove Group doesn't just present opportunities: it organizes relationships, understands potential and turns conversations into concrete next steps.
